A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Clustering-Based Validation Splits for Model Selection under Domain Shift. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization. The dataset inconsistency in v3's new convergence experiment is a localized reporting issue.

before.justification: v2 reports original DG and UDA experiments on six datasets, training-distribution controls, and appendix ablations and MMD analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds experiments comparing clustering solutions and assessing sensitivity to the number of classes.

M1.justification: The constrained kernel k-means method, linear-programming assignments, class and optional domain constraints, and Nyström approximation are retained. Algorithm 1 reformats the existing procedure. The expanded kernel discussion and suggested domain-informed features do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: The six original DG/UDA datasets and tasks remain. Section 5.7 adds a synthetic multiclass partitioning scenario on Humpbacks, replacing the original labels with 1–500 balanced synthetic classes. The additional application examples in Appendix A are proposals, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.6 newly evaluates Wecker et al. (2020) against the proposed clustering algorithm; v2 discussed this method only as prior work. The comparator membership in the original benchmark and ablation tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New auxiliary protocols include a matched linear-kernel, label-only clustering comparison with holdout fraction 0.5, and synthetic-label generation on 8,000 Humpbacks examples with three pairwise MMD measurements. The pooled median/IQR-normalized, symmetrical-log analysis is removed. Original benchmark settings and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 5.6–5.7 add substantive tests of optimization quality versus greedy assignments and sensitivity to class count. The pooled cross-dataset correlation analysis is removed. Existing VLCS and Camelyon17 ablations are retained and moved into the main text. The convergence experiment's dataset is unresolved: its text says VLCS, while Figure 2 says Humpbacks.

E5.justification: The original three-trial reporting, standard errors, and confidence-interval rule remain. The new convergence study reports 20 random initializations and boxplots, while pooled correlation tests disappear. Section 5.4 newly justifies omitting error bars, but its claim of negligible errors conflicts with the accuracy uncertainties reported in Table 1.

E6.justification: v3 removes the pooled Spearman correlation of approximately 0.63 and log-scaled Pearson correlation of 0.61. It adds convergence-loss distributions and class-count results: Table 5 reports MMD(T,V) decreasing from 0.221 to 0.129 between 1 and 500 synthetic classes. All matched benchmark, control, and appendix result tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: v3 explicitly assumes finite class and domain sets and adds discussion of the characteristic-kernel condition for distinguishing distributions. The central MMD/k-means equivalence, LP integrality argument, convergence argument, and appendix derivation remain unchanged. Their new theorem and proposition labels do not represent new proofs.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain constrained clustering for model selection, convergence guarantees, optional domain metadata, improved DG/UDA selection, and an MMD–accuracy association. The abstract drops the numerical pooled correlation coefficient but retains the qualitative association claim; the introduction's contribution list and conclusion preserve the same scope.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussions, including kernel-dependent assumptions, feature selection, class-count limitations, nominal-distribution tradeoffs, and access to target-domain data. It acknowledges that bandwidth 1 was inappropriate and that clustering and leave-one-domain-out results overlap within uncertainty. The earlier discussion excluding synthetic spurious-correlation benchmarks is removed.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies domain stratification of random/mix-up splits, class-balanced validation and test accuracy, evaluation-domain partitioning, and reliance on DomainBed defaults. It also identifies use of Wecker's official implementation. The original hyperparameter and Humpbacks processing/architecture tables are retained, so these disclosures do not establish changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands beyond bibliographic updates. v3 acknowledges prior MMD/k-means connections in França et al. and Ohl et al., develops the comparison with Wecker, and contrasts its approach with target-aware validation selection. Additional discussions connect the work to kernel choice, convergence complexity, and domain-informed representations.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the narrative, separating prior work, preliminaries, method, experiments, and limitations into standalone sections. It expands methodological explanations, moves existing ablation discussions into the main text, adds a feature-extraction appendix, and removes the earlier illustrative spurious-correlation discussion.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column journal layout, with reformatted tables and a separate Algorithm 1 display. The pooled correlation figure is removed; convergence boxplots and a class-count table are added. Existing appendix Tables 6–7 become main-text Tables 2–3, while their results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added optimization comparison, class-count analysis, experimental disclosures, and explicit kernel/applicability limitations provide a limited net improvement in interpretability and practical guidance. The core benchmark results and proofs remain stable. Benefits are tempered by removal of the pooled correlation evidence and new reporting problems: the VLCS/Humpbacks mismatch in Section 5.6/Figure 2 and the error-bar justification conflicting with Table 1.
